angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 223,320 km at 27.86 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 35.8963 +/- 0.0169 mas (same row, RUWE 1.18): 27.86 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.321 +/- 0.014 solar radii from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5799 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract): 223,320 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.325 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5799 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3452 +/- 96 K from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5799 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5799 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5799.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.937, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
